Hey! Your PR title `add browser tool powered by browser-use` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

Based on the search results, I found a related PR:

**PR #7302:** "Added in-built browser tools using playwright and a parallel playwright node process using spawn for bun-playwright issues"
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/7302

**Why it's related:** This is a previous attempt to add browser tool functionality to the agent. However, that implementation used Playwright, while the current PR (#35844) uses `browser-use`. The new approach appears to be a replacement/improvement using a different tool and implementation strategy.

No other duplicate PRs found for the specific `browser-use` feature implementation.
Thanks for updating your PR! It now meets our contributing guidelines. :+1:
Thanks but no — this is a suspicious attachment from an unverified contributor. The fix for a CLI binary should be a PR or a code diff, not a zip file from a stranger. Please close this.
Superseded by #35848, which is correctly based on v2.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:

- #24445: Windows 11 long-running TUI sessions accumulate large JS heap — same platform and pattern of memory growth over extended sessions
- #33213: Long-running `opencode serve` accumulates anonymous JS heap/swap with 26.8 GiB peak — very similar unbounded memory growth profile
- #35107: Memory keeps growing until the bun process is killed — same root symptom
- #20695: Memory Megathread — general tracking issue for memory-related reports
- #33742: OpenCode v1.17.10 crashes with Bun segfault on Windows — similar crash on Windows

If your issue is already covered by one of the above, please add a comment there with your diagnostics rather than opening a new report. If it is distinct (e.g., the `Illegal instruction` panic at a specific address is the primary issue rather than just OOM), please clarify what differs so maintainers can triage it separately.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #35240: Server keeps stale `project.worktree` after project folder is renamed — same root cause (DB record not updated, same SQLite workaround), and nearly identical symptoms.
- #30697: Project still opens old path after move/delete — same user-facing behavior where re-adding a project at a new path still resolves to the old one.

If your issue is distinct (e.g. specific to the desktop re-add flow rather than rename/move), please add that context so it can be triaged separately.

> ⚠️ **Security warning — do not download `opencode_fix.zip` in the comment above**

The user **@guvubededome** who posted that attachment:

- Account created on 2026-07-08 (only hours before this issue was opened)
- Zero repositories, zero followers, zero following, no bio, no public activity
- Replied **21 seconds** after the issue was created

This is a classic supply-chain phishing pattern: a throwaway account monitoring new issues and dropping a "fix" attachment that is almost certainly malicious malware.

**Do not download, extract, or run `opencode_fix.zip`.** I have reported the account to GitHub for abuse. Legitimate fixes will always come through a PR reviewed by maintainers, never a zip attachment from a brand-new account in an issue comment.

If you already downloaded/ran it, treat your machine as compromised: disconnect from network, run a full AV scan, rotate credentials that may have been on that machine.
